assessment: The incumbent provides staffed key access and telephone/in-person reservations; eleven groups obtained weekly bookings (H4-O1). Its eight-week target remains unproven: total needs and acceptable alternatives are unmeasured, three conflicts occurred, and observed administration averaged 127.5 minutes/week (H4-O3, H4-O4, H4-O6). The strongest account is that familiar repeating allocations provide some predictability, while incomplete demand records and inconsistent booking records limit coordination. A concrete limit to a simple spare-capacity explanation is H4-O3: six declined requests concentrated on Tuesday/Thursday evenings. Aggregate 68% reservation and late/missed sessions do not establish usable capacity in those windows (H4-O2); unspecified equipment also prevents treating rooms as interchangeable (H4-O5).

openings.claim: Inherited 90-minute allocations may exclude feasible rehearsals by mismatching actual duration, time-window, and equipment requirements.
openings.delta: Distinguish reallocatable time from genuine peak-time or piano scarcity before changing bookings.
openings.prediction: If allocation mismatch matters, a demand-informed schedule will meet more stated needs within accepted windows using existing room-hours. If peak/equipment scarcity dominates, unmet needs will persist despite rearrangement.
openings.probe: Use short contact conversations to record weekly needs, minimum usable durations, acceptable windows, and equipment. Compare current bookings with a proposed schedule protecting both performances and each requested weekly 60-minute entitlement. Count only accepted alternatives; check feasibility before implementation.
assumptions: Contacts can represent group needs accurately.
Shorter rehearsals are useful only when explicitly accepted.

openings.claim: One authoritative desk calendar, with dated change entries and a read-back of room/date/time to the contact, may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Make the online copy traceable to confirmed desk changes while retaining telephone and in-person access.
openings.prediction: Calendar-disagreement conflicts should decline; the other two conflicts may persist if their causes differ. Added recording could increase administration.
openings.probe: For eight weeks, record conflict causes and weekly administration minutes alongside change entries. Compare divergence-related conflicts separately from other conflicting expectations; assess the total conflict and two-hour administration targets.
assumptions: Desk staff and volunteer can share the authoritative record during existing staffed hours.
No software purchase or participant account is required.
